_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: Sam recorded himself using SkyView for seven minutes and narrating what went wrong, and a new video-context skill turned that recording into frames and a transcript entirely on his own laptop — nothing left the machine. Two problems were then measured in a real browser rather than guessed at. The search list shifts down by exactly one row when the row of picked-course chips grows onto a second line, so the course you were about to click moves out from under the pointer; the fix shipped the day before preserved the list's scrolling but not its position on screen, which is why the complaint survived it. And double-clicking a course strands you: the page swaps to the discipline workspace without telling the browser, so Back does nothing, the menu disagrees with the screen, and coming back wipes every course you had picked. Sam also retracted one of his own reports on camera once he found the feature working — that retraction is recorded as prominently as the defects, so nobody undoes a good fix. He ruled on three things: Enter should close the search panel, double-click should open the course outline, and the chip row should reserve its space because stability wins. The course outline is still the top priority and has now been planned three times without being built.

items.text: This is the one thing blocking the course outline's skill layer. You ruled that agency skill statements come from all three sources — published agency standards, ACE exhibits and the MAP team. What happens when the three disagree about the same certification? The pilot is an AWS welding certification. Everything else in the outline can be built without this answer.

Sam's ruling: Enter closes the search panel, the sort chip moves to the list's top right, and an Enter button takes the sort button's place — keyboard and button both working. Note this REVERSES ruling 6 from the same morning, which he flagged himself. Ship it with the chip-row fix below, since both are the same panel.

The search dropdown drops 36 pixels — one row height — when the chip row wraps at the fourth pick, so the row under the pointer becomes a different row. Reserve the chip row's space (Sam: stability wins) and tighten chips horizontally to fit more per row. Contrast is fine; target size is the limit, and the remove button is already at the 24px AA floor. Guard it by asserting the list's screen position across four picks, not by counting bar rows.

Double-clicking a course strands you: discipline() repaints over SkyView without updating the address, so Back does nothing, the view menu disagrees with the screen, a refresh silently discards the work, and returning rebuilds the map and loses every pick. Give the discipline view a route, make the round trip keep the picks, and drop the stale 'prototype v1' label from the masthead while you are there.

You ruled 'All three' on where agency skill statements come from — published agency standards, ACE exhibits, and entered by the MAP team — and flagged it for follow-up. The open question is what wins when the three disagree about the same certification. That answer shapes the course outline's comparison panel, so the next session will need it early.

Three welding merge candidates are queued for a faculty reviewer, not for a session: Introduction to Welding (24 colleges) absorbing Introduction to the Welding Processes (2) and Intro-Welding Processes (1), and the Intermediate Shielded Metal Arc Welding pair behind it. A fourth pair shares a title but is flagged as NOT mergeable — one is credit and one is noncredit, which makes them different courses. kb/merge_candidates/2026-09-05/report.md.

The re-mint approval view is designed and routed through Governance, not built. You approve candidates and the cron applies them; there is no fire button, because a re-mint cannot be undone the way an ordinary correction can. Worth a read before it is built — it names what each candidate must show you, including what the plan was checked against, which is exactly the thing that was missing this week.

Build the course outline on double-click: a layered panel with the MAP-Generated label on every synthetic field, proficiency levels on the course and on each skill, thin skills kept with a confidence chip, and a certification-first way in beside the course-first one. Double-click currently opens the discipline work surface, so split it — a course opens the outline, empty ground keeps today's behavior.

Build the re-mint approval queue against the four-item checklist in its decision record: a register row owning the approval, the surface mapped the moment the first write lands, an insert-only rollback, and a test asserting the view writes approvals and nothing else.

The panel's new Similar courses list reads course levels out of titles, which is the only place we hold them — 44% of Welding's 512 titles say Beginning, Intermediate or Advanced and the rest are listed last rather than guessed at. When the course outline ships with a real level field, feed it back here so the ladder stops depending on wording.
